The spatial predator mean z is decreasing and cannot tend to a nonzero value: a positive Neumann heat-kernel bound would force persistent w>0 and negative z′. The positive Neumann spectral gap forces v/z→1 as t→∞. The prey stable resolvent B=d_u∂xx−λ implies w/z→βψ_a where ψ_a=(−B)^{-1}1_(0,a). Substituting into z′ gives (1/z)′→αβ s_a and thus t z→1/(αβ s_a), with uniform predator and prey profiles. Direct differentiation and Neumann/interface matching verify ψ_a is piecewise hyperbolic as stated; independent SymPy finds zero function and derivative jumps and the average s_a. The thin-zone coefficient s_a/a→κ/(λ tanh(κ L)), yielding lim_{a↓0}lim_{t→∞}t∫_0^a v dx=√(λ d_u)tanh(L√(λ/d_u))/(αβ). This is an iterated limit, not uniform in a. Key semigroup domination requires δ chosen with αδ below prey/predator gaps, available at each fixed positive a.
